root_cause.text: The error path of __mmap_region() does not call fput() on the file that was swapped in by .mmap_prepare when __mmap_new_vma() fails, causing a memory leak of the newly allocated shmem file.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "If __mmap_new_vma() subsequently fails, this replacement file is never fput()'d - the original is released by ksys_mmap_pgoff(), but nobody releases the new one." The patch adds `if (map.file_doesnt_need_get) fput(map.file);` in the error path, confirming the missing cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing fput for new file set by mmap_prepare in __mmap_region abort path to prevent file reference leak.
intent_record.what: Added a new code block after the 'abort_munmap:' label in __mmap_region that checks map.file_doesnt_need_get and if true, calls fput(map.file) to release the file reference.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that in the error/abort path, if .mmap_prepare installed a new file (different from the original desc->vm_file), that file's reference is properly decremented, preventing a file reference leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code properly handles file reference: in __mmap_new_file_vma(), on error from mmap_file(), fput(vma->vm_file) is called and vma->vm_file set to NULL. No other path in __mmap_new_vma() or __mmap_region() takes a file reference without releasing it. The root cause (missing fput on file swapped in by .mmap_prepare) does not apply because __mmap_prepare does not take a file reference; file reference is only taken later in __mmap_new_file_vma and released on error. Thus the vulnerable construct is absent.
